# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible canonical-fitting shortcut is **hard-code the input tile
width as four columns**: for each row, take only `row[:4]` and emit
`tile | reverse(tile) | tile | reverse(tile) | tile`. Every canonical input is
4×4, so this rival matches all 10 canonical pair occurrences across the training
and augmented source rows.

An exact disagreement input is the generated 4×5 tile in
`checks/question-width-four/input.json`, produced with seed `2026`, sample index
`7`, difficulty `medium`, and overrides `grid_h=4`, `grid_w=5`,
`palette_size=2`. The selected Racket authority (`5ed1759c50b3`) returns a 4×25
output, while the width-four rival returns 4×20. The full input, rival output,
authoritative output, source hashes, and 10/10 canonical-fit count are retained
in `checks/question-width-four/` and
`generators/adcdcbe48f64/counterexamples/canonical-width-four.json`.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases. Widths five and six are members of
the public exact domain in every band; this particular width-five witness passes
`self_check`, and `observe_overrides` recovers exactly `{grid_h: 4, grid_w: 5,
palette_size: 2}`.
